tools.description: Start here to resolve a product name to its url_name, then call get_software for details (structured license, pricing, rating, links) or get_alternatives for its alternatives.
After search_software or get_alternatives returned a url_name, or when the user pastes an alternativeto.net/software/... URL.
Explore a category or feature across the catalog rather than alternatives to one product.
When the user asks for alternatives to a known product; chain from search_software's url_name.

PeerSpot head-to-head comparison of two products: category ranking, average rating (out of 10), reviews sentiment and review count per product, category mindshare, and per-theme sentiment scores with editorial summaries and reviewer quotes (ROI, customer service, scalability, stability, room for improvement, setup cost, valuable features). Order of the two slugs does not matter.

Call first when starting from a company name or ticker: it returns every other identifier, so one call here makes the rest of this provider addressable. Also the only place peers and secondary listings are published.
To compare where to run a given model: prices and measured speed per provider. Needs a model slug from search_models.
Call to understand how a firm invests before weighting what it says about a company. The profile is derived from its own letters rather than from marketing material.

Call for what was said on the call, attributed and timed. The speaker mapping is what makes it worth more than the raw text: management's prepared remarks and an analyst's question can be told apart, and the Q&A boundary is given rather than guessed.
When you have a model slug from search_models (or a pasted /models/{slug} URL) and need the full benchmark record.
Cite a paper found with `search_papers`, `list_category` or `get_paper`.
Look up one paper by identifier or URL. Use `get_bibtex` for a citation entry and `harvest_records` for the license.
Bulk or incremental synchronisation of arXiv metadata by date window, or the only surface that states a paper's license. For topical search use `search_papers`.
Browse what was announced in a category, or walk a month's submissions. Identifiers feed `get_paper` and `get_bibtex`.
Discover valid `set` values for `harvest_records` and category codes for `list_category`.

Find papers by topic, title, author or category, or find the arXiv identifier that `get_paper`, `get_bibtex` and the listing functions take. Citing or replicating papers are not an arXiv concept: arXiv serves no citation graph.

Read video metadata, description and any available transcript. Transcript availability is not guaranteed. Not channel listings, comments or timestamped captions. Scrape pricing per successful attempt: 1 credit base, plus 4 for audio and 4 for video (5 for either, 9 for both), before other Scrape surcharges. The wrapper adds no charge; underlying Scrape requests are billed separately at their current rate. Invalid YouTube Markdown may trigger one fresh Scrape call.
